```{r fonctions}

tab_contingence <- function(x,titre=NULL,...){
  x<- addmargins(as.matrix(x), FUN = list(Total = sum), quiet = TRUE)

  # Renommer la dernière ligne et la dernière colonne
  rownames(x)[nrow(x)] <- "Total"
  colnames(x)[ncol(x)] <- "Total"
  x %>% 
    kable() %>% 
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width = F, 
      position = "center") 
}

tableau_contingence_latex <- function(x,titre=NULL,position = 'center',...){
  x %>% 
    kable(caption = titre,
        align = "c",
        ...) |> 
  kable_styling(latex_options =  c("HOLD_position","scale_down","striped","hover"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = position) |> 
    row_spec(0,
           background = "cornflowerblue",
           color = "white",
           italic = FALSE,
           bold = TRUE) %>% 
    column_spec(1,
                background = "blanchedalmond",
                color = "black",
                italic = TRUE)

}


graph_pointhtml <- function(tab, titre_legende = "Légende", titre = NULL, sous_titre = NULL, xlab = "x", ylab = "y", abs, ord, quali_var = NULL, cond = FALSE, ...) {
  # color ou fill, pas les deux
  aes_color_fill <- if (!is.null(quali_var)) {
    aes_string(x = abs, y = ord, color = "quali_var")
  } else {
    aes_string(x = abs, y = ord)
  }
  
  tab %>% 
    ggplot(aes_string(x = abs, y = ord, color = "quali_var")) +
    geom_point(aes_string(x = abs, y = ord), show.legend = cond) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = titre, subtitle = sous_titre,
         color = titre_legende) +  # Modifier le titre de la légende
    theme(plot.title = element_text(color = "black", hjust = 0.5, face = "bold.italic"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "red", hjust = 0.5, face = "bold.italic"),
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey"),
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey"),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey"),
          axis.title.x = element_text(color = "red", face = "bold.italic"),
          axis.title.y = element_text(color = "red", face = "bold.italic", ...),
          axis.text.x = element_text(color = "darkblue", face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "darkblue", face = "italic"),
          legend.text = element_text(color = "darkblue", face = "italic"),
          legend.title = element_text( color = "black", hjust = 0.5, face = "bold.italic"))
}



contrigraph <- function(ACP,choice,axes=1,xlab=NULL,ylab="Contributions (en %)",titre="Etude des contributions",sous_titre =NULL,...){
  fviz_contrib(ACP, choice = choice, axes = axes,...)+
    labs(x=xlab,
         y=ylab,
         title = titre ,
         subtitle = sous_titre)+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(color ="black",
                                    hjust = 0.5,
                                    face = "bold.italic"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "red",
                                       hjust = 0.5,
                                       face = "bold.italic"),
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
          axis.title.x = element_text(color = "red",
                                      face = "bold.italic"),
          axis.title.y = element_text(color = "red",
                                      face = "bold.italic",...),
          axis.text.x = element_text(color = "darkblue",
                                     face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "darkblue",
                                     face = "italic"),
          legend.text = element_text(color = "darkblue",
                                     face = "italic"),
          legend.title =element_text(color = "black",hjust = 0.5,
                                     face = "bold.italic"))
}







ACPscreenplot <- function(ACP,titre="Etude des inerties",sous_titre=NULL,...){
  fviz_screeplot(ACP,addlabels = TRUE)+
    labs(title = titre,
         subtitle = sous_titre,
         x = "Dimensions",
         y = "Pourcentage") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                    hjust = 0.5,
                                    face = "bold.italic"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "red",
                                       hjust = 0.5,
                                       face = "bold.italic"),
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
          axis.title.x = element_text(color = "red",
                                      face = "bold.italic"),
          axis.title.y = element_text(color = "red",
                                      face = "bold.italic",...),
          axis.text.x = element_text(color = "darkblue",
                                     face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "darkblue",
                                     face = "italic"),
          legend.text = element_text(color = "darkblue",
                                     face = "italic"),
          legend.title = element_text(color = "black", hjust = 0.5,
                                      face = "bold.italic"),
                   panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey"),panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA,colour = "white"),rect = element_rect(fill = NA,colour = "white"))
}







mon_theme <- theme(plot.title = element_text(color ="black",
                                             hjust = 0.5,
                                             face = "bold.italic"),
                   plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "red",
                                                hjust = 0.5,
                                                face = "bold.italic"),
                   panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),

                   panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey",linetype = "dotted"),
                   legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "white",color = "white"),
                   legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white"))

matrice_cor <- function(tab,titre = NULL){
  corrplot(cor(tab),type = "upper",addCoef.col = "black",
           tl.cex = 0.75,number.cex = 0.75,tl.col = "black",
           method = "square",
           title = titre,
           diag = FALSE)
  
}
```

## Popularité des morceaux {-}

```{r}
#Les variables charts représentent des classements, le fait que ces variables soient quantitatives pourraient poser des problèmes d'interprétation, ainsi, il faut trouver un moyen de les rendre interprétable

# Utiliser des fonctions crées à partir de dplyr si on les utilise dans des commmandes issues de dplyr
top_chart <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x == 0 ~ 'pas classé',
    between(x, 1, 10) ~ 'Top 10',
    between(x, 11, 50) ~ 'Top 50',
    between(x, 51, 200) ~ 'Top 200',
    between(x, 101, 1000000) ~ '> 200',
    TRUE ~ '?'
  )
}

df_stat_des <- df_stat_des |> 
  mutate(across(ends_with("charts"), top_chart, .names = "top_{.col}")) |> 
  # on créer de nouvelles dont le nom sera "top_{.col}" en appliquant la fonction
  # top_chart au variable dont le nom se termine par charts 
  select(everything())#on sélectionne toutes les variables de df (car on attribue le nouveau df à df, il faut donc garder toutes les anciennes variables et simplement ajouter les nouvelles)

```

# ACP {-}

## Présentation de l'analyse par composantes principales {-}


```{r echo=FALSE}

df_ACP<-read_delim("data_frame_dossier/spotify-2023_nettoyer.csv",delim = ",",
               locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))

df_ACP <- clean_names(df_ACP,"snake")
df_ACP$streams <- as.double(df_ACP$streams)
df_ACP$key <- as.factor(df_ACP$key)
df_ACP$mode <- as.factor(df_ACP$mode)
df_ACP <- df_ACP[-575,]
#names(which(df$track_name |> table()>1))

```


```{r echo=FALSE}
#Combinons le nom de la musique et des artistes

df_ACP <- df_ACP[,-1]




top_chart <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x == 0 ~ 'pas classé',
    between(x, 1, 10) ~ 'Top 5',
    between(x, 11, 20) ~ 'Top 20',
    between(x, 21,50) ~ 'Top 50',
    between(x, 51, 1000) ~ '>50',
    TRUE ~ '?'
  )
}
  
df_ACP <- df_ACP |> 
  mutate(across(ends_with("charts"), top_chart, .names = "top{.col}")) |> 
  # on créer de nouvelles dont le nom sera "top_{.col}" en appliquant la fonction
  # top_chart au variable dont le nom se termine par charts 
  select(everything())


quanti <- which(sapply(df_ACP,FUN = is.numeric)==TRUE)
quali <- which(sapply(df_ACP,FUN = is.character)==TRUE)
quali <- append(quali,which(sapply(df_ACP,is.factor)==TRUE))
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
quanti_sup<-c(6,8,11,13,14)
colnames(df_ACP)[25] <- "top_spotify"
```


```{r echo=FALSE}
resacp<-PCA(df_ACP,quali.sup=c(quali),quanti.sup=quanti_sup,graph = FALSE)
```


```{r}
dfAFC$saison <- ifelse(dfAFC$released_month_char %in% c("décembre","janvier","février"),"hiver",
                    ifelse(dfAFC$released_month_char %in% c("mars","avril","mai"),"printemps",
                    ifelse(dfAFC$released_month_char %in% c("juin","juillet","août"),"été",
                    ifelse(dfAFC$released_month_char %in% c("octobre","septembre","novembre"),"automne",NA))))
```

```{r}

tab %>% kable(align="c") |> 
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped","hover","HOLD_position"),position = "center",full_width = FALSE) |> 
  column_spec(1,background = "cornflowerblue",color="white",bold=T,italic=T)
```


```{r}
round(chi2$expected,3) |> tableau_contingence_latex()
```


```{r}
contrib<-chi2$residuals^2 %>% 
  proportions() %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  round(4)*100

colnames(contrib)[5]<-"Total"
rownames(contrib)[6]<-"Total"
contrib %>% kable() %>%
   kable_styling( 
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
     bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")
    ) %>%
  column_spec(2,color=ifelse(contrib[,1]<5,"green",
                             ifelse(contrib[,1]<10,"orange","red"))) %>%
  column_spec(3,color=ifelse(contrib[,2]<5,"green",
                             ifelse(contrib[,2]<10,"orange","red"))) %>%
  column_spec(4,color=ifelse(contrib[,3]<5,"green",
                             ifelse(contrib[,3]<10,"orange","red"))) %>%
  column_spec(5,color=ifelse(contrib[,4]<5,"green",
                             ifelse(contrib[,4]<10,"orange","red"))) %>%
  column_spec(6,color=ifelse(contrib[,5]<5,"green",
                             ifelse(contrib[,5]<10,"orange","red"))) |> 
  row_spec(0,bold=TRUE,background = "cornflowerblue",color = "white",italic = T) |> 
  column_spec(1,bold=TRUE,background = "blanchedalmond",color = "black",italic = T)
```

# ACM {-}



```{r ajout_var_df_ACM}

#Les variables charts représentent des classements, le fait que ces variables soient quantitatives pourraient poser des problèmes d'interprétation, ainsi, il faut trouver un moyen de les rendre interprétable

# Utiliser des fonctions crées à partir de dplyr si on les utilise dans des commmandes issues de dplyr
top_chart <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x == 0 ~ 'pas classé',
    between(x, 1, 5) ~ 'Top 5',
    between(x, 5.1, 20) ~ 'Top 20',
    between(x, 20.0001, 50) ~ 'Top 50',
    between(x, 50.000001, 80000) ~ '>50',
    TRUE ~ '?'
  )
}


df <- df |> 
  mutate(saison = case_when(released_month_char %in%
                              c("décembre","janvier","février")~"hiver",
                            released_month_char %in%
                              c("mars","avril","mai")~"printemps",
                            released_month_char %in% c("juin","juillet","août")~"été",
                            TRUE~"automne"),.after = released_month_char) |>
  select(everything())


# Créarion d'une variable featuring
df <- df |> 
  mutate(feat = case_when(artist_count>1~"oui",
                          TRUE~"non"),.after = artist_count) |> 
  select(everything())



 
# Les clés n'étant pas forcément connu de tous, on va rendre cette variable plus claire.

df <- df |> 
  mutate(tonalite = case_when(key %in% c("C","C#","D","D#")~"registre grave",
                              key %in% c("E","F","F#","G")~"registre moyen",
                              key %in% c("A","A#","B","G#")~"registre aigu",
                              TRUE~"registre ?"),.after = key) |> 
  select(everything())


normaliserx100 <- function(x){
  round(((x-min(x))/(max(x)-min(x)))*100,4)
}
#Création de variable qualitative ordonnée pour plusieurs caractéristiques des musiques




df <- df |> 
  mutate(across(ends_with("charts"), top_chart, .names = "top_{.col}")) |> 
  # on créer de nouvelles dont le nom sera "top_{.col}" en appliquant la fonction
  # top_chart au variable dont le nom se termine par charts 
  select(everything())#on sélectionne toutes les variables de df (car on attribue le nouveau df à df, il faut donc garder toutes les anciennes variables et simplement ajouter les nouvelles)




df <-  df |> 
  mutate(across(c(bpm,streams),normaliserx100,.names = "{.col}_normx100")) |> 
  select(everything())

df <- df |> 
  mutate(across(c(bpm_normx100,ends_with("percent")),~case_when(.>=75~4,
                                                .>=50~3,
                                                .>=25~2,
                                               TRUE~1),.names = "ind_{.col}")) |> 
  mutate(across(starts_with("ind_"),as.factor)) |> 
  select(everything())
  



colnames(df)[40] <- "speechiness"
colnames(df)[39] <- "liveness"
colnames(df)[38] <- "instrumentalness"
colnames(df)[37] <- "acousticness"
colnames(df)[36] <- "energy"
colnames(df)[35] <- "valence"
colnames(df)[34] <- "danceability"
colnames(df)[33] <- "rythme_bpm"

colnames(df)[27] <- "top_spotify"
colnames(df)[28] <- "top_apple"
colnames(df)[29] <- "top_deezer"
colnames(df)[30] <- "top_shazam"



rm(cor_df,df_stat_des,data_stream,vec_couleur,MFM,Description,Gestion_NA,mois)
quanti <- which(sapply(df,FUN = is.numeric)==TRUE)
quali <- which(sapply(df,FUN = is.character)==TRUE)
quali <- append(quali,which(sapply(df,is.factor)==TRUE))



quali_sup <- c(2,5,6,17:19,27:30)



res_ACM <- MCA(df,quali.sup = quali_sup,quanti.sup = quanti,
               graph = FALSE,ncp = Inf)



```

<center>**Que disent les parangons ?**</center>

```{r fig.height=1,fig.width=3}
tab_par %>% kable() %>%
  kable_styling( 
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center", font_size = "11px",
    latex_options = c("striped", "hover")
  )  %>% pack_rows(
    "Cluster 1", 1, length(par1)
  ) %>% pack_rows(
    "Cluster 2", length(par1) +1 , length(par1) + length(par2)
  ) %>% pack_rows(
    "Cluster 3", length(par1)+ length(par2)  +1 , length(par1) + length(par2) + length(par3)
  ) %>% pack_rows(
    "Cluster 4", length(par1) + length(par2) + length(par3) + 1, length(par1) + length(par2) + length(par3)+  length(par4)
  ) %>% pack_rows(
    "Cluster 5", length(par1) + length(par2) + length(par3) + length(par4) +1 , length(par1) + length(par2) + length(par3) +length(par4) + length(par5)
  ) |> 
  row_spec(0,background = "cornflowerblue",color = "white") |> 
  column_spec(1,background = "blanchedalmond",color = "black")  
  
  
```
